paragraphs: Madison AI sells a platform that turns a government's own files and systems into an AI assistant for staff. The pages describe drafting staff reports, looking up code and zoning by parcel, researching voting history, and analyzing contracts against procurement standards. The homepage states that the product makes work easier in local government and water districts.

The site says the engine was created by Washoe County and OnStrategy. The about page names Washoe County as a co-founder and an equity partner rather than only a customer. The site names the City of Reno, Washoe County, and the Northern Nevada Regional Transportation Commission among government clients.

Deployment is described as taking about four weeks, with full deployment in less than sixty days. The homepage says the product is used by 65+ local governments and counting. A time study by the City of Reno is cited as reducing staff report production by more than 75%.

quote.text: Off-the-shelf tools have value, but only purpose-built AI from their data and records can actually tackle the specialized and nuanced work governments complete every day.
